Identify the basic blocks and construct a flow graph for the below code snippet. for (i = 2; i <= n; i++) { a[i] = TRUE; } count = 0; s = sqrt(n); for (i = 2; i <= s; i++) { if (a[i] == TRUE) { count++; for (j = 2 * i; j <= n; j = j + i) { a[j] = FALSE; } } }

Design a Syntax-Directed Definition (SDD) that generates the prefix form of expressions while simultaneously performing type checking. Your design should clearly define the attributes used for prefix generation and type information, specify semantic rules for each production, handle type compatibility between operands, and incorporate automatic type promotion wherever necessary. (6 marks)

Then, apply your SDD to construct the annotated parse tree for the expression (a + b) * (c - d / e). In your answer, show the computed prefix representation at each node, Illustrate the evaluation of attributes from bottom to top and determine the final prefix expression. (4 marks)

Analyse the following C program and identify all possible code optimization techniques that can be applied to improve its efficiency. Clearly explain where and why each optimization technique can be applied. Finally, write the fully optimized version of the given code. int a, b, c, d, result, x, y; // Assume a, b, c, d, x, y are assigned values elsewhere a = b + c; x = b + c; y = a + x; if (y == 2 * a) { result = (d * 0) + 5; goto end; } else { result = 10; goto end; } result = 1; end

An industrial automation system monitors and controls machine operations using sensor inputs. The system uses variables such as T1, T2 (temperature readings), P1, P2 (pressure values), and a constant K for calibration. The control logic combines these inputs to compute an output signal. The expression used in the system is: (T1 + T2) * (P1 - P2) + (T1 * P1/K) + 100. As a compiler designer, generate the three-address code sequence for the above expression. Also represent the expression using quadruples and triples.

Explain the various issues encountered during the code generation phase of a compiler. Illustrate each issue with a suitable example to show how it affects the generation of efficient and correct assembly or machine code.

For each of the following errors, identify in which phase the compiler will detect it and why it cannot be detected earlier: i) x = y + z; (where z is not declared) (2 Marks) ii) x = y ** 5; (invalid operator) (2 Marks) iii) if (a + b > c) x = 10 (missing semicolon) (2 Marks) iv) int x = "hello"; (type mismatch) (2 Marks) v) a = b = c = 5; (if language does not support chained assignment) (2 Marks)
b. Write a Lex program to check and display whether the given input contains digits, alphabets, or special characters. (5 marks)

A software company is developing a lightweight database query processor for an embedded system that supports a simplified SQL-like language. The processor must be capable of parsing queries that include selecting multiple attributes from a table and filtering results using conditional expressions combined with logical operators. The syntax of this query language is defined by the grammar: Q → select L from id where C; L → L, id; L → id; C → C and C; C → id < id; C → id > id. To efficiently parse such queries, the development team has decided to use an SLR parsing approach. a. Construct the canonical collection of LR(0) item sets for the above grammar. (6 Marks)
b. Compute the FOLLOW sets required for SLR parser construction. (3 Marks)
c. Construct the SLR parsing table (ACTION and GOTO) for the grammar. Clearly indicate any shift-reduce or reduce-reduce conflicts, if present. (6 Marks)

A national meteorological center uses a 10-year-old serial Fortran application to generate daily weather forecasts. The application simulates atmospheric physics using a 3D grid, computing heat transfer, fluid dynamics, and pressure changes for millions of cells. With the demand for higher resolution (smaller grid cells), the simulation now takes 30 hours to complete for a 24-hour forecast. The model is failing to meet its 6-hour runtime constraint, making the forecasts useless. The original developers have left, leaving behind 500,000 lines of complex, poorly documented "legacy" code. a. Identify two primary reasons why the serial application is no longer adequate based on the case study. (3 Marks)
b. Explain why simply buying a faster single-core CPU (processor) will not solve the 30-hour simulation bottleneck. (3 Marks)
c. Identify the most likely candidate in the code for parallelization, and explain why. (3 Marks)
d. Apply the concept of automatic parallelization to a loop-based computation and explain how the compiler identifies and parallelizes independent operations. (3 Marks)
e. In a real-world scenario where automatic parallelization is applied to legacy code, identify potential risks and explain their impact on program output and efficiency (3 Marks)

A compiler is processing a program that implements a simple queue initialization and insertion logic using conditional statements and a loop. The given high-level code is: SIZE=10; front = -1; rear = -1; for (int i=1; i<= 5; i++) if (front == -1) { front = 0; rear = 0; printf("Queue initialized"); } else if (rear == SIZE - 1) printf("Queue Overflow"); else { rear++; printf("Inserted into queue"); } As part of the intermediate code generation phase, perform the following tasks for the given program: a Convert the program into three-address code (TAC) using appropriate labels and conditional jumps. (5 marks)
b. Identify the leaders and divide the program into basic blocks. (5 marks)
c. Construct the control flow graph (flow graph) showing the execution flow between the basic blocks, clearly indicating all possible transitions. (5 marks)
